name: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī
summary: Ascetic traditionist and jurist of Baghdad, a great collector of the language, author of Gharīb al-ḥadīth; his family came from Merv.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī describes al-Ḥarbī as versed in letters, a great collector of the language, an ascetic, a memoriser of ḥadīth and learned in law, and names his Gharīb al-ḥadīth among his many books. His family came from Merv; he explained his name al-Ḥarbī by the quarter of al-Ḥarbiyya in Baghdad, where he lived.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 276–278
